title: Temperature-Dependent Formation and Release of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons During Coal Gangue Pyrolysis
content: Coal gangue stockpiling poses severe environmental risks, particularly through spontaneous combustion that releases hazardous organic pollutants. In this study, a controllable tube furnace pyrolysis system was employed to investigate the temperature-dependent formation and release of 16 priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) from five coal gangue samples (CG01–CG05) across temperatures ranging from 200 °C to 600 °C under a N2 atmosphere. The results revealed a distinct non-monotonic, unimodal temperature dependence for total PAH concentrations (Σ16PAHs). The mean Σ16PAHs concentration increased sharply from 162.47 μg kg⁻¹ at 200 °C to a maximum of 1533.96 μg kg⁻¹ at 400 °C, and subsequently declined to 806.72 μg kg⁻¹ at 600 °C. This trend indicates that ~400 °C represents a critical thermal window favoring active PAH generation and release, whereas elevated temperatures (500–600 °C) promote secondary cracking, oxidation, and high-temperature transformation. Ring-number distribution analysis showed that 4-ring PAHs were the dominant fraction across all peak temperatures. Furthermore, significant sample-dependent variations were observed (e.g., CG01 consistently exhibited the highest concentrations, while CG05 showed the lowest), highlighting the influence of intrinsic coal gangue heterogeneity—such as initial organic matter composition and mineral matrix effects—on PAH evolution. These findings provide critical data for assessing and mitigating environmental and health risks associated with the thermal treatment and spontaneous combustion of coal gangue.
